title: Roles and Separation of Duties
html:
Goal: tell the console's three layers apart: global roles, permissions and project roles; sign in as each of the five seeded accounts and see what each can do; approve a self-registered account as administrator; check the workspace release policy gated the organiser preset; and understand who performs each sign-off on the flywheel, and why it can never be the same person.

Prerequisites

  • the Setup chapter done: you can open ConsoleUrl/v3, have signed in to console V3 as admin, and the left rail shows every module.
  • The passwords of your team's five accounts from the organiser at hand: admin, developer, biz-owner, release-ops, sme.
  • Every administrative action in this chapter (approving an account, inspecting permissions, checking the release policy) is done by admin. These actions decide "who may do what, and what may ship". They are platform governance and belong with nobody who later builds or signs.

1. Two layers: roles and permissions

The console has four global roles:

Role (UI label) Purpose Notes
admin (Administrator) Platform administrator Holds every permission; manages accounts, workspaces and the release policy, and can see every project's data. The built-in admin comes from configuration and can never be locked out
steward (Organization admin) Organization structure Manages accounts, departments, projects and workspaces, but does not see project data and holds no grant or project membership itself. Suits an IT or organization manager who only sets up the structure; not used in this workshop
operator (Operator) Release operator Approves and runs releases, signs release decisions, approves waivers. Deliberately does not hold agents.deploy: an operator releases what someone else built rather than editing prompts or code
member (Member) Member Builds agents, writes criteria, starts evaluations and release requests

On top of the roles sits a set of permissions (16 keys). Each role has a default set, and an administrator can grant or revoke individual keys per account (one chip click per key on the Agent permissions card of the account detail, see section 5; inside a project they are adjusted through the project role instead, see section 4 of Teams and Roles):

Permission key What it allows member default operator default
agents.deploy / agents.import / agents.delete / agents.convert Deploy, import, delete, convert agents Yes No
eval.run Start evaluation runs (they invoke agents and cost money) Yes Yes
promotion.request Request a promotion Yes Yes
promotion.approve Review and execute promotions No Yes
identity.manage / identity.grant / memory.manage Manage connections and identity, grant one's own access, manage memory resources Yes identity.grant only
criteria.manage Edit and publish criteria tables, maintain golden-set items Yes Yes
criteria.sign Sign a criteria table No No
golden.admit Seed the golden set, admit new samples No No
judge.calibrate Decide judge calibration, issue annotation links No No
waiver.approve Approve or reject waivers No Yes
release.sign Sign, block and roll back releases; move an agent onto live / candidate endpoints No Yes

Note the three in bold: criteria.sign, golden.admit and judge.calibrate come with no non-admin role; an administrator grants them to named people. They decide what "good" means, which samples count, and whether a judge can be trusted. That is ownership of the standard, so it must rest with a named business owner, not with "every member" or "every operator".

Project roles

Global roles and permissions say who an account is on the platform. The console can also split work into projects and give each member a project role inside a project. Within a project, what an account can do is decided by its role there (an administrator can still adjust single keys per member). The platform ships seven project role templates:

Project role Keys it carries Typical holder
Project owner project_owner Manages the project's members, sees the project's audit and cost views, shares resources, plus every member build key; no sign-off or approval key Project manager
Developer developer Read and write in the project, plus the 10 member defaults developer
Business owner biz_owner Read and write in the project, eval.run, criteria.manage, criteria.sign, golden.admit, judge.calibrate, identity.grant biz-owner
Release ops release_ops Read and write in the project, the 7 operator defaults, plus reviewing MCP tool lists (mcp.approve) release-ops
Domain expert sme Uses the project only (chat, feedback, labels) plus identity.grant sme
Tool steward tool_steward Uses the project only, plus mcp.approve Security or platform team
Viewer viewer Read only Observers, auditors

There is also Inherits global role: the member's keys follow their global role and permissions, and every member of the default project default holds it. This chapter uses only the default project, so the permissions in section 3 are the global ones; the chapter Teams and duties sets up several projects and assigns project roles.

The five seeded accounts follow this model:

Account Role Granted on top of defaults Duty in this workshop
admin admin All (by role) Platform governance: accounts, workspaces, release policy
developer member criteria.manage, agents.deploy, eval.run (already member defaults) Builds and deploys agents, drafts and publishes criteria, starts evaluations; the requester of every release
biz-owner member criteria.sign, golden.admit, judge.calibrate Business owner: signs criteria, curates the golden set, decides whether a judge is calibrated
release-ops operator release.sign, waiver.approve (already operator defaults) Release operator: signs or blocks releases, approves waivers, rolls back
sme member None Subject-matter expert: the second annotator in judge calibration

sme and developer hold the same global permissions (member defaults already include criteria.manage, eval.run, agents.deploy); the difference only shows in their project roles. The server enforces separation of duties by account (the account id, not a display name that can change): the same account cannot both request and sign. The table in section 7 lists every rule.

2. Prepare several browser sessions

The console keeps your sign-in in a session cookie, so one browser profile holds one signed-in account at a time. To stay signed in as several accounts:

  • Recommended: several browser profiles (Chrome / Edge "Add profile", Firefox Multi-Account Containers), or two or three different browsers side by side.
  • Works: one normal window plus one private / incognito / InPrivate window. Note that in Chrome and Edge all incognito windows share one cookie jar, so normal plus incognito gives you at most two accounts at once.
  • Also works: switch accounts in one window with the Sign out icon button at the top right of the top bar, to the right of the username.

In the steps below, the normal window stays signed in as admin throughout.

3. Sign in as each seeded account and compare

3.1 Sign in as developer

  1. In a second browser session open ConsoleUrl/v3 (a new browser profile starts in V2, hence the /v3), on the Sign in tab enter developer and its password, and click Sign in.

    You land on the Command center, with Launchpad and a V3 badge at the top left. The first time this browser opens /v3, the Console tour starts on its own; click Skip (you can reopen it later from the Help (question mark) button in the top bar → Take the tour).

  2. Look at the left rail. At the top are four fixed entries: Command center, Agents, Chat, Release gate; below them, under Modules, the module groups, folded (click a group name to expand it; the number on the right is how many modules it holds). A member starts in the essentials mode, which shows only: Agent development (Architect assistant, New agent, Agent IDE, Knowledge Bases, Context layer), Agent runtime (Releases, Issue box, Observability), Agent evaluation (Intent view, Standards), Learn (Video introductions).

In the image: 1 the four fixed entries Command center, Agents, Chat, Release gate; 2 the essential groups under Modules (Agent development, Agent runtime, Agent evaluation, Learn); 3 the Show every module button at the bottom.

  1. Click Show every module at the bottom of the rail.

    Expected result: the button changes to Show the everyday modules only, the group counts become Agent development 6, Agent runtime 8, Agent evaluation 9, Learn 1, and these 13 modules are added: Registry, Environments, Memory, Governance, My authorizations, Gateway tools, Evaluation overview, Data center, Evaluation tasks, Online evaluation, Evaluators, A/B experiments, Skill Lab. The Configuration group (User Management, Projects, Network profiles and so on) and Spend & alerts under Agent runtime are still absent, because they are shown to administrators only.

    The mode is remembered by the browser, not by the account. If you switched it in this browser profile before, you already see every module and the button at the bottom reads Show the everyday modules only; skip this step.

  2. Open ConsoleUrl/v3/users in the address bar.

    Expected result: the page title is User Management (subtitle administrator only), and the body says Administrator access required and "This module manages console accounts and is limited to administrators." The rail mode is only a view filter; this is the real permission boundary: knowing the address does not help, the backend refuses.

  3. In a new tab of the same session open ConsoleUrl/api/auth/status.

    Expected result: the JSON identity of this session, with "username": "developer", "role": "member", and a permissions list of the 10 member defaults (see the table in 3.3).

3.2 Sign in as biz-owner, release-ops, sme in turn

In the second session click the Sign out icon button at the top right, then sign in as biz-owner, release-ops and sme with their passwords, opening ConsoleUrl/api/auth/status each time.

Expected result: all three see the same rail as developer (no Configuration group, no Spend & alerts); only role and permissions differ.

3.3 Reference table

Account role permissions (from /api/auth/status, alphabetical)
admin admin All 16
developer member agents.convert, agents.delete, agents.deploy, agents.import, criteria.manage, eval.run, identity.grant, identity.manage, memory.manage, promotion.request
biz-owner member The 10 above, plus criteria.sign, golden.admit, judge.calibrate
release-ops operator criteria.manage, eval.run, identity.grant, promotion.approve, promotion.request, release.sign, waiver.approve
sme member The same 10 as developer

release-ops holds no agents.* permission at all: it can see the agents but cannot deploy, change or delete them. That is the operator role by design.

4. Approve a self-registered account as administrator

Self-registration is on in this console, but a new account cannot sign in until an administrator approves it. You play a new colleague, then let them in as admin.

4.1 Self-registration (the new colleague)

  1. In the second session click the Sign out icon button at the top right, and on the sign-in page switch to the Register tab (title Create an account, "Register with your company email. An administrator reviews new accounts before they can sign in.").

  2. Fill in:

    Field Value Rule
    Username trainee-<yourname> (the measured run used trainee-alex) 3-32 characters: letters, digits, dot, underscore or hyphen
    Company email trainee-<yourname>@example.com Public mailbox providers (Gmail, QQ, 163, Outlook…) are not accepted
    Password / Confirm password Pick one and write it down (same value in both fields) At least 8 characters

  3. Click Create account.

    Expected result: the card title changes to Waiting for approval with "trainee-alex was submitted for review. An administrator has to approve it before you can sign in; the 7-day validity starts then.", followed by Email (the one you entered), Status Pending approval, and a Go to sign in button.

In the image: 1 the Waiting for approval heading; 2 Status reads Pending approval; 3 the Go to sign in button.

  1. Click Go to sign in and try to sign in with the new account.

    Expected result: sign-in fails with "This account is waiting for administrator approval." A pending account gets no session, so a public console address grants nothing extra.

4.2 Approval (admin)

Back in the normal window where admin is signed in:

  1. In the rail, under Modules, expand Configuration and click User Management (/v3/users). A notice at the top says "1 account is waiting for approval.", and the Awaiting approval figure is 1.

  2. Click Show them in the notice (the same as choosing Pending approval in the status filter above the list). The list now shows only your trainee-... account, with Status Pending approval and Valid until "Starts on approval".

    The V3 Command center does not list registrations; a pending account is flagged only in User Management.

In the image: 1 the Show them button in the pending notice, which switches the status filter to Pending approval (red box); 2 the Approve button at the right of the row.

  1. Click Approve at the right of that row. The Approve account dialog opens with default already checked under Workspaces. Keep it checked and click Approve at the bottom of the dialog.

    The console has only the default project for now, so the dialog shows workspaces only. Once Teams and duties has created several projects, this dialog also offers a Role (member or operator) and Projects (Add project, then pick a project and its project role), with the workspaces folded into Legacy workspace grants (advanced), so one approval puts a new colleague straight into the right projects.

    Expected result: a toast "trainee-... was approved.". The account is no longer pending, so it drops out of the current filter; switch the status filter back to All and the row shows Role Member, Status Active, Workspaces default, and Valid until the days left followed by the expiry date 7 days out. Right after approval it reads 6 day(s) left · <approval date plus 7 days> (measured: approved on 17 October, shown as 6 day(s) left · 2026-10-24): a partial day is not counted.

In the image: 1 default, already selected under Workspaces; 2 the Approve button at the bottom of the dialog.

  1. Back in the second session, sign in as trainee-....

    Expected result: sign-in succeeds, the rail has no Configuration group, and the workspace selector at the top right shows Default · us-east-1. ConsoleUrl/api/auth/status shows "role": "member" and the 10 member defaults, with no sign-off permission at all.

If you deselect default when approving, the dialog warns "No workspace selected: the account will be approved but cannot open any environment until one is granted."; if you click Approve anyway, that account signs in to a No workspace granted page ("This account has no workspace yet, so there is no environment to show. Ask a console administrator to grant one from User Management."). Workspace grants can also be changed later in the Workspace access card of the account detail.

5. Inspect the seeded accounts' permissions

Still on User Management in the admin window, switch the status filter back to All and click the biz-owner row to open its detail (the address is /v3/users?view=detail&user=biz-owner):

  • To the right of the title are four account actions: Disable, Reset password, Force sign-out, Delete.
  • The figures at the top: Status Active, Role Member, Valid until Never expires, and Last sign-in. The Account overview card lists the username, email, registration time, Created by and Account source (Local account for the seeded accounts).
  • Agent permissions card: one chip per permission; a highlighted chip with a check mark is granted, and the small monospace text to the right of the label is the permission key. criteria.sign, golden.admit and judge.calibrate are all granted for biz-owner.
  • Workspace access card: default is granted.

Click ← User Management at the top left of the page to go back, open developer, release-ops and sme in turn, and compare with the table in 3.3.

Look, do not click. A click on a chip in Agent permissions or Workspace access grants or revokes it immediately. Each chip shows its label on the left and the permission key in monospace on the right, e.g. Sign criteria criteria.sign, Admit to golden set golden.admit, Decide calibration judge.calibrate. release-ops' role shows as Operator (operator) in the list and the detail.

The button on the Role card only toggles between member and administrator. To create an operator or organization admin account, use Add user at the top right of the User Management list: an administrator creating an account directly can pick Member, Operator, Administrator or Organization admin, and the account needs no approval. Do not click Make administrator on release-ops: an administrator holds every permission, and the separation-of-duties demonstration would be gone.

In the image: 1 Sign criteria criteria.sign; 2 Admit to golden set golden.admit; 3 Decide calibration judge.calibrate, all checked, i.e. granted; 4 Default, granted under Workspace access. The monospace text to the right of each label is the permission key.

Force sign-out

Someone left the team, lost a laptop, or you just revoked a permission and want them to sign in again now: click Force sign-out in the account detail. The confirmation says every session of the account ends on its next request and they must sign in again, while password, role and access stay the same. Confirm with Force sign-out and a toast reads "<username> has been signed out everywhere".

In the image: 1 the title Force sign-out?; 2 the Force sign-out confirm button.

Try it on the trainee-... you approved: after confirming, refresh the second session and it lands on the sign-in page; sign in again. Do not do this to the five seeded accounts, or you interrupt your teammates.

6. Check the release policy: preset to gated (admin)

The release policy is set per workspace, decides how a new version reaches production, and only an administrator can change it:

Field (Release policy card) Key Workshop value Meaning
Release mode release_mode gated (Gated — a new version waits on the gate) The default is direct (Direct — a deploy goes straight to production). In gated mode a deploy lands on the candidate endpoint and opens a pending release record; only after the gate passes and a second person signs does the live endpoint move to the new version. A rollback just re-points live at the previous version
Calibration valid for (days) calibration.period_days 30 A judge calibration lapses after this long and must be redone. Allowed 7–365, default 90
Required judge–human κ calibration.kappa_floor 0.6 Below this judge-to-human agreement (Cohen's κ) a judge cannot be declared calibrated. Allowed 0.2–0.95; 0.6 is "substantial" agreement. When unset the server decides with 0.61 and the card shows 0.6; here 0.6 is written explicitly
Ask to confirm above (USD) eval_cost_confirm_usd 5 An evaluation estimated above this asks the person to confirm the cost. The server also uses 5 USD when unset. When an estimate is above this line the UI marks it "Above the confirm line — starting it confirms the cost", and clicking Run the gate is the confirmation
Refuse above (USD) eval_cost_max_usd 20 An evaluation estimated above this is refused unless an administrator starts it. Unset means no limit

When the organiser deployed the environment, the setup script signed in as admin and wrote the values in the table above into the release policy of the default workspace, so this step checks them and changes nothing.

In console V3 these fields live in the Release policy card of the Release gate view (/v3/standards?view=release) on the rail's Modules → Agent evaluation → Standards page, visible to administrators only. Note that this is not the fixed Release gate entry at the top of the rail (/v3/gate); that page has no release policy card. But every view of the Standards page works on one active agent, and there is no agent yet, so the page only says "No active agent yet. Create and deploy one first; a standard is always a standard for something." So for now read the release policy endpoint directly in the browser:

  1. In the browser window where admin is signed in, open a new tab at ConsoleUrl/api/release-policies/default. This is the same endpoint the console reads the release policy from (GET /api/release-policies/{workspace_id}): the browser sends admin's session cookie by itself, and when a request carries no X-Workspace header the backend uses the default workspace for an administrator.

    Expected result: the page shows JSON with "workspace_id":"default" and "tier":"dev", and policy is:

    json
    {
  "release_mode": "gated",
  "calibration": {"period_days": 30, "kappa_floor": 0.6},
  "eval_cost_confirm_usd": 5.0,
  "eval_cost_max_usd": 20.0
}

    The backend stores the amounts as floats, so they show as 5.0 and 20.0. effective is these values laid over the DEV tier defaults (min_eval_score, smoke_prompts and so on), with release_mode gated as well. Chrome and Edge show the JSON as one line of plain text (tick Pretty-print at the top of the page to break it into lines); Firefox shows it in its JSON viewer.

  2. The write is journaled: action release_policy.update, actor admin (the setup script signs in as admin before writing). The Observe chapter shows it when it reads the decision history.

Once the Build chapter has deployed the first agent, open the Standards page as admin, pick the Release gate view, and the Release policy card shows the same values; from then on you can also change them in the card and click Save. Other accounts do not see that card, but in the same view the foot of the Endpoints stat tile shows the current release mode, "Gated — a new version waits on the gate". Before the Evaluate chapter starts evaluating, admin checks the cost guard on this card once more.

In the image: 1 RELEASE MODE Gated — a new version waits on the gate; 2 CALIBRATION VALID FOR (DAYS) 30; 3 REQUIRED JUDGE-HUMAN K 0.6; 4 ASK TO CONFIRM ABOVE (USD) 5; 5 REFUSE ABOVE (USD) 20; 6 Save after a change.

Gating only applies to an agent that has been moved onto live / candidate endpoints. After each agent's first deploy, release-ops, who holds release.sign, clicks Move to live/candidate in the Release gate view of the Standards page (the Release chapter). Until then, deploys still take effect directly.

7. Who does what, and why

The table lists every action in this workshop that needs a second pair of eyes. The server compares accounts (an account that changes its display name is still the same person) and refuses a request that breaks a rule, with the error code in parentheses:

Action Who Permission Server rule Why
Draft and publish the criteria table developer criteria.manage — The builder knows best what the agent can be tested on
Sign the criteria table biz-owner criteria.sign The signer cannot be the version's creator or last editor (criteria.self_sign); administrators are exempt, so by convention admin does not sign either The business owner accepts the standard; a builder does not set the exam and then grade it
Seed the golden set, admit new samples biz-owner golden.admit The holdout is written once, by the seed; an admitted sample must carry a human-written expected answer Which samples count is part of the standard
Human labels for judge calibration developer + sme Any member, but only the task's named annotators A calibration task needs at least two independent annotators Agreement between two people is the baseline the judge is measured against
Decide whether a judge is calibrated biz-owner judge.calibrate The decider cannot be any of the task's annotators, its adjudicator, or the issuer of one of its annotation links, administrators included (calibration.own_labels); below the κ floor "aligned" is refused (calibration.not_supported) Whoever wrote the evidence does not rule on it
Start the release evaluation developer eval.run An estimate above the confirm line needs confirmation; above the maximum it is refused Evaluations cost money, and the amount must be visible
Sign / block / roll back a release release-ops release.sign Only a release whose gate verdict is PASS can be signed (release.gate_not_passed); the signer cannot be the release requester, i.e. whoever deployed that version (release.self_sign), administrators included A builder cannot wave their own change into production
Request a waiver developer Any member Must name a reason, a risk owner and an expiry at most 30 days out; red lines are never waived (waiver.redline) Asking is not deciding
Approve a waiver release-ops waiver.approve The approver cannot be the requester (waiver.self_approve) Accepting a risk takes a second person
Review a cross-workspace promotion release-ops promotion.approve The reviewer cannot be the requester (promotion.self_approval) Same reason; this workshop has a single workspace and does not use it
Set the release policy admin Administrator Administrators only It decides what may ship, and when
Approve registrations, grant workspaces admin Administrator Only administrators reach User Management Who may enter the environment is platform governance 
flowchart LR
  DEV[developer<br/>drafts criteria · deploys · starts evaluations] -->|publishes criteria| BIZ[biz-owner<br/>signs criteria · golden set · decides calibration]
  DEV -->|labels| CAL[Judge calibration task]
  SME[sme<br/>second annotator] -->|labels| CAL
  CAL -->|evidence| BIZ
  DEV -->|deploys to candidate| GATE[Release gate]
  GATE -->|PASS| OPS[release-ops<br/>signs release · approves waivers · rolls back]
  ADM[admin<br/>accounts · workspaces · release policy] -.governs.-> GATE

Checklist

  • You can name the four global roles, tell them from project roles, and say why criteria.sign, golden.admit, judge.calibrate are granted to named people only
  • Signed in once each as developer, biz-owner, release-ops, sme; /api/auth/status returned the role and permissions of section 3.3
  • As a member, /v3/users showed Administrator access required
  • trainee-<yourname> was approved by admin: status Active, role Member, workspace default, and it can sign in
  • Workspace default has release policy gated, calibration valid for 30 days, κ floor 0.6, confirm line 5 USD, maximum 20 USD
  • Using the table in section 7, you can explain who performs each sign-off and what the server refuses

Troubleshooting

Symptom Cause Fix
After signing in as a second account, the first window switched to it too Both windows share one cookie jar (same browser profile, or two incognito windows) Use another browser profile or another browser, see section 2
Registering says "Use your company email — public mailbox providers are not accepted." A public mailbox domain such as Gmail, QQ, 163 or Outlook Use @example.com
Registering says "That username is taken or reserved." The username exists, or it is the built-in administrator's admin Pick another trainee-... username
Sign-in says "This account is waiting for administrator approval." Not approved yet Have admin approve it as in 4.2
Sign-in says "This account is disabled. Contact an administrator." Reject was clicked during approval (rejecting disables the account), or it was disabled admin clicks Enable for the account in User Management
The new account is not in User Management The list was not refreshed, or the status filter is neither All nor Pending approval Click Refresh at the top right, adjust the filter
Opening ConsoleUrl/api/release-policies/default returns {"code":"auth.required",...} (HTTP 401) This browser window is not signed in, or the session expired In the same window open ConsoleUrl/v3 and sign in as admin first, then open the address again
policy comes back as {}, or release_mode is not gated The release policy preset did not take effect when the organiser deployed Tell the organiser; once the Build chapter has deployed the first agent, admin can also fill in the Release policy card under Standards → Release gate with the values of section 6 and Save
Save on the Release policy card fails with calibration.bad_policy A value out of range: period_days must be a whole number 7–365, kappa_floor between 0.2 and 0.95, amounts not negative Retry with the values in section 6

3.2 Sign in as biz-owner, release-ops, sme in turn
4. Approve a self-registered account as administrator
6. Check the release policy: preset to gated (admin)
